3. Questions on complexity classes:
a) Prove that P< NPand P ccoNP.
[When the complement of a problem belongs to NP then the problem itself belongs to
coNP |
SOLUTION: The class P is closed under complementation: if L is a language in P, then the
complement of L is also in P. You can see this by taking any polynomial-time decider for L
and switching the accept and reject states; this new machine now decides the complement
of L and does so in polynomial time.
A language L is in co-NP iff its complement is in NP. So consider any language L € P. The
complement of L is also in P, so the complement of L is therefore in NP (because P & NP).
Therefore, L is in co-NP. Consequently, P © co-NP.
